contribution: Methods for empirically analyzing market power, demand and differentiated-product markets (structural empirical industrial organization)
rationale: The BLP framework (1995) is a central, heavily cited tool in industrial organization, antitrust, merger review and trade economics. Industrial organization has not been honored since Tirole in 2014. Recent prizes went to institutions (2024) and innovation-driven growth (2025), which leaves room for a methods-heavy applied microeconomics award. Among alternatives (e.g., Kiyotaki and Moore on financial frictions, or Blanchard), this seems the most plausible single bet, though any one prediction carries low certainty.
